concept.name: Corporate-action adjustment
concept.definition: The point-in-time treatment of splits, dividends, mergers, spinoffs, and other issuer events in prices, positions, orders, and cash flows.
concept.intuition: It controls what information the model receives and in what numerical representation.
concept.mechanics: On the event's effective timestamp, adjust quantities and reference prices or book the economic distribution without using later-known terms early.
concept.failure_modes: Fitting the operation on the full dataset leaks future information; revisions, outliers, and missing values can also distort results.
concept.misconceptions: A cleaner or rescaled dataset is not automatically more truthful; transformations must preserve timing and economic meaning.
concept.example: A 2-for-1 split changes 100 shares at a $60 basis into 200 shares at a $30 per-share basis without creating profit.
